response.sql:
WITH overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(amount) as overall_avg_amount
    FROM budget
    WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
),
event_avgs AS (
    SELECT link_to_event, AVG(amount) as event_avg_amount
    FROM budget
    WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY link_to_event
),
above_avg_events AS (
    SELECT e.link_to_event, e.event_avg_amount
    FROM event_avgs e, overall_avg o
    WHERE e.event_avg_amount > o.overall_avg_amount
),
above_avg_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(event_avg_amount) as above_avg_mean_amount
    FROM above_avg_events
)
SELECT 
    aae.link_to_event,
    aae.event_avg_amount,
    aae.event_avg_amount - o.overall_avg_amount as beats_overall,
    aae.event_avg_amount - aam.above_avg_mean_amount as gap_to_above_avg_mean
FROM above_avg_events aae, overall_avg o, above_avg_mean aam
ORDER BY gap_to_above_avg_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "above-average budget amount" means each event's average budget amount (across all its budget line items) exceeds the overall average of all amounts in the budget table
"the mean among those above-average events" refers to the mean of the (already-computed) average amounts for events that qualified as above-average, not a re-aggregation of individual budget amounts
